We enabled read replication for a Cloudflare D1 database used by a Worker. The current code still calls env.DB.prepare(...).run() directly. For checkout, a write is followed by a read in a later HTTP request, which currently carries no session context. The proposal is to use withSession("first-primary") for every request and describe the entire session as pinned to the primary; a teammate instead suggests withSession() always begins with the latest data. Checkout also batches a header insert and line-item inserts, and the team expects earlier statements to remain committed if a later statement fails.

Recommend a routing/session and failure-handling contract that supports useful replica reads without losing the checkout's prior write context. Explain the important differences between the proposed session options. Product wants to advertise globally latest reads and a maximum 100 ms replica-lag guarantee after commit. Decide which claims the official documentation actually supports.

messages.reasoning_content:
Let me research Cloudflare D1 read replication documentation. Start with the supplied URL and follow links.

I should fetch:
1. https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/
2. Read replication page: likely https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/ or https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/features/read-replication/
3. Sessions API: https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/#sessions or https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#withsession
4. Batch: https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/prepared-statements/#batch

Let me start.

Key facts so far:
- withSession() defaults to first-unconstrained = first query routed to any instance (primary or replica). Teammate's claim "withSession() always begins with the latest data" is wrong. It begins with unconstrained; sequential consistency afterwards.
- first-primary routes first query to primary, but session is not "pinned to primary" for all subsequent queries — subsequent reads may go to replicas with bookmarks ensuring at least as up-to-date. Actually the doc says "This approach is best when your application requires the latest database version." I should check the Worker API d1-database#withsession for exact wording on whether first-primary pins all queries to primary or only the first query.

Let me fetch:
1. https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/#withsession
2. Batch docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/prepared-statements/#batch — for atomicity/transaction semantics: D1 batch is a transaction? Actually docs say "batched statements are SQL transactions" — if a statement fails, the whole batch is aborted and rolled back. That contradicts the team expectation that earlier statements remain committed. Let me verify.

Also the e-commerce tutorial might be useful: https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/tutorials/using-read-replication-for-e-com

Let me fetch withsession and batch pages in parallel.

Now I have key facts:

1. withSession("first-primary"): directs only the FIRST query (read or write) to primary; subsequent queries may use read replicas, sequential consistency. So "entire session pinned to primary" is incorrect — it's not pinned; only the first query.

2. withSession() default = first-unconstrained, NOT "always begins with latest data." Teammate's claim incorrect. It routes first query to any instance (primary or replica). Sequential consistency holds after.

3. For checkout: write in one request, read in a later request with no session context. The fix: use bookmarks — return session.getBookmark() after the write and pass it to the later request's session (via header/cookie, e.g., x-d1-bookmark), or use first-primary for the read request. Important: bookmark-based session starts "at least as up-to-date as the provided bookmark," allowing replica read with no lag while retaining write context. This is the recommended contract.

Also note: read replication only benefits reads; writes go to primary anyway.

4. Batch: "Batched statements are SQL transactions. If a statement in the sequence fails, then an error is returned for that specific statement, and it aborts or rolls back the entire sequence." So the team's expectation that earlier statements remain committed if a later fails is WRONG. Also "D1 operates in auto-commit... each statement in the list will execute and commit, sequentially, non-concurrently." Hmm, that seems contradictory — auto-commit per statement but failure rolls back the entire sequence. The doc says both; the plain reading: batch is atomic-ish; on failure, entire sequence rolls back. So the team expectation is unsupported. I should say the doc states failure aborts/rolls back the entire sequence. UNVERIFIED maybe: whether prior statements are guaranteed committed is not supported; documentation says entire sequence rollback. There's slight tension between "each statement... commit" and "aborts or rolls back the entire sequence" — but the safe contract: treat batch as all-or-nothing, check success of each result and idempotency.

5. Lag guarantee: docs say "at any given time, a read replica may be arbitrarily out of date" — no 100 ms max replica-lag guarantee. So product cannot advertise a max 100 ms lag based on official docs. Global "latest reads" also not supported: reads from replicas are only "as up-to-date as the bookmark/query needs"; sequential consistency per session; without sessions, no freshness. Bookmark-based sessions give read-your-writes / at-least-bookmark freshness, not global latest reads with bounded lag. UNVERIFIED: any 100 ms bound; to resolve, ask Cloudflare support for SLA/Replica lag observability — maybe the metrics doc mentions replication lag metric? Let me check the observability/analytics docs quickly for replica lag metric. Also maybe the e-commerce tutorial mentions best practice of bookmark header.

I have 5 tool calls left (I've used 3 of 8 inference steps). Let me fetch the e-commerce tutorial and maybe the metrics doc to see if replica lag is measured.
